gates: Read the complete recipe contract before domain or release work
Copied databases only for candidate, audit, shadow and benchmark work
Frozen semantic gold, exact hashes/ID sets, immutability, rollback and activation gates stay mandatory
Run affected existing PHP fixture suites under 128 MB; bridge tests in its supported environment
Release only to SFenton/EverShelf with explicit authorization

always: Keep secrets out of evidence; do not inspect or retain official Cookidoo steps or unapproved provider content.
Backend data ownership, immutable versions and explicit activation boundaries remain authoritative.

research: Locate existing API/SQL/ontology mechanisms before proposing replacements; lexical similarity is not identity proof.
Use copied fixtures for proposed experiments and distinguish source facts from unmeasured runtime behavior.
implementation: Read the full recipe contract; preserve bounded SQL, source provenance and proposal-only boundaries.
validation: Use affected existing fixture suites with required memory, semantic-gold, hash, shadow and rollback checks.
release: Only the SFenton/EverShelf fork is a release target; verify remote identity and explicit authorization.

commands.runtime: Use an isolated supported container when host PHP/provider dependencies are unavailable
